title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Liang Chen
description:
Context: production running workloads showed occasional request starvation and elevated p99 latency during tail spike events when many short and long requests were co-located. This PR contains a set of scheduler and queueing changes for the continuous-batcher aimed at improving fairness across request classes, preventing starvation of low-throughput routes, and introducing configurable timeouts to bound waiting time for batched slots. Motivation: make batching decisions robust to skewed traffic patterns (mix of 4-token fast requests and 2048-token long requests) and reduce latency tail at minimal throughput regression. Key changes: 1) introduce dual-queue scheduler: short-request queue (latency-first) and batch-throughput queue (throughput-first) with proportional slot allocation; 2) implement per-route starvation detector that increments priority if requests wait longer than starvation_threshold_ms; 3) add configurable max_wait_ms and per-slot timeout handlers to close slots and flush partial batches to avoid indefinite waits; 4) refine fairness weights calculation to account for recent serviced token-count (token-aware fairness) instead of only request-count; 5) add metrics and tracing hooks (batch.wait_time_ms, batch.evict_reason, scheduler.queue_length_by_class) for observability; 6) safety net: when high variance detected, automatically fall back to emergency small-batch policy. Implementation notes: scheduler rewritten in scheduler.go to separate queueing policy from batch formation; introduced scheduler_config.proto updates and runtime flags (continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms, continuous_batcher.starvation_threshold_ms, continuous_batcher.fairness_decay_window_ms). The description below summarizes diffs, testing, and rollout plan. Changes made (high level): - scheduler/scheduler.go: new dual-queue logic, starvation detector, timeout handlers - scheduler/policy.go: fairness weight calculation refactor and unit tests - runtime/config.proto: schema for new tuning knobs - serving/metrics.go: added batch-level metrics and tags - tests/continuous_batcher_integration_test.go: added stress scenarios and regression checks - tools/benchmarks/bench_scheduler.py: new microbench harness for queueing scenarios Benchmarks: microbench results (on p4d.24xlarge equivalent) show p99 latency improvement for short requests from 220ms -> 145ms (approx -34%), while throughput for long-request mixes decreased by ~2.1% in worst-case synthetic stress. End-to-end canary on dedicated cluster reduced customer-observed tail SLO violations from 3.7% to 0.9% for mixed workloads. Checklist:
- [x] design doc reviewed by runtime team
- [x] unit tests for policy and starvation detector
- [x] integration tests (stress mix)
- [x] metrics and dashboards updated
- [x] canary rollout to 5% of dedicated capacity
- [x] rollback plan prepared (revert flag + emergency small-batch policy) Testing and verification: ran full CI (build + unit + integration), ran bench_scheduler microbench across different mix ratios (short-only, long-only, 70/30 mix). Also executed a 24h canary on a dedicated pool with synthetic traffic and monitored batch.evict_reason and queue length histograms. No memory leaks detected in valgrind runs. Rollout plan: staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated monitoring alerts on increase of skipped_tokens_ratio or throughput drop >5% for >10m. If elevated errors or latency regressions occur, runtime flag continuous_batcher.force_small_batch=true will be flipped and changes reverted. Related: ENG-3421 tracks follow-up to expose tunables in console; ENG-3489 tracks further tuning of fairness decay window.

review_comments: Asha Patel (reviewer): Can you explain how starvation_threshold_ms interacts with max_wait_ms? If starvation increments priority it might still exceed max_wait and be evicted — please clarify the intended interaction.

Liang Chen (author): Good question — the starvation detector increases the class priority which biases slot allocation; max_wait_ms is an absolute cap on how long a request may block before being flushed. The idea is to reduce chances of hitting max_wait by proactively prioritizing starved classes. Added comment in scheduler.go and unit test to cover edge case.

Diego Martinez (reviewer): Suggest adding a metric for 'priority_escalations' so we can correlate escalations with SLO improvements. Also concerned about potential thundering herd when many requests escalate at once.
Liang Chen (author): Added priority_escalations counter and added backoff jitter to escalation path to avoid herd effect. See policy.go changes.

Maya Rios (reviewer): Integration test shows intermittent failure under heavy long-request load — observed partial batches being evicted too frequently which reduced throughput. Can we add an adaptive grace window?

Liang Chen (author): Added emergency_small_batch policy that triggers when evict_reason==PARTIAL_BATCH_HIGH_RATE and throughput drop observed; this is part of the safety net. Also tuned decay window to 60s by default.
Asha Patel (reviewer): lgtm after addressing metrics and adding canary rollout plan. Please ensure console exposes the tunables before broad rollout.
Liang Chen (author): Added ENG-3421 to expose tunables in console; will follow up in separate PR. Thanks for the review.

release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler: dual-queue fairness, starvation prevention, configurable max wait/timeouts, new batch-level metrics. Expected p99 latency reduction for short requests in mixed workloads; small throughput tradeoff in extreme long-request mixes. Tunables added for safe rollout.
